leadText:
A Fisher (Japanese: つりびと Fisher) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that first debuted in the Generation I games. Prior to Generation VIII, they were known as Fisherman, except in Pokémon Stadium and , which also used "Fisher" due to text space concerns. They are typically depicted as middle-aged men with rods, reels, and fishing gear, with a used as a lure. However, younger Fishermen have been seen in , and in , female Fishers were introduced.

In the Japanese version of , they are depicted smoking, as fishermen smoking is a common stereotype in Japan. The cigarette was removed in international releases.

They specialize in Pokémon that can be caught via fishing. In most core series games, there is a Fisherman who will fight the player with a full team made up entirely of . In the in Galar, Fishers use both Pokémon and those that may benefit from rain.

In Generation VII, they keep their Pokémon in Lure Balls, while in Generation VIII, they keep them in Dive Balls instead.

In Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, Fishermen will award three s along with prize money upon being defeated.

==In animation==
 
Marie's grandfather from Type Casting is a fisherman.

Several fishermen competed in the Seaking Catching Day competition in Hook, Line, and Stinker

Several fishermen competed in the Whirl Cup in Octillery The Outcast and Dueling Heroes, notably and .

Wings Alexander disguised himself as a fisherman in Throwing in the Noctowl.

A self-proclaimed "fishing god" named Sullivan appeared in Whiscash and Ash, where he was hunting for a nicknamed Nero.

An old fisherman traded his for the that accidentally caught in a flashback in Judgment Day!.

A fisherman used a to battle a in Buizel Your Way Out Of This!, but lost.

An old fisherman appeared in If the Scarf Fits, Wear It!.

A fisherman appeared in Entei's Fierce Battle Cry!.

==== ====
 
Wilton, 's uncle, is a Fisherman. He taught her how to fish and gave her a for transportation.

==== ====
A Fisherman was one of many visiting the in Weavile Wobbles But It Won't Fall Down.

==== ====
In Beedrill Prepares, it was revealed that after the defeat of Team Aqua, ex- became a Fisherman.

==== ====
A Fisherman appeared as a background character in Deprogramming Porygon-Z, where he was part of a group of people who entered the after Palmer had his assistants open the gates.

==== ====

==== ====
A Fisherman appeared walking by the fountain in Santalune City in Kangaskhan...Kangascan't.
